small_guidance:
- Add a `triton.autotune` sweep over `BLOCK_OC ∈ {32,64,128}`, `BLOCK_HW ∈ {64,128,256}`, `BLOCK_IC ∈ {32,64}`, `num_warps ∈ {4,8}`, `num_stages ∈ {2,3,4}` keyed on `(OC, OHW, IC)` — current single 64/128/32 @ 4w/2s is almost certainly not optimal for the 514×514 output.
- Eliminate the global `atomic_add` into `pooled` by tiling so each `(n, oc)` is owned by a single program along HW (persistent loop over HW tiles in registers, then one non-atomic store), or by accumulating in shared mem; atomics on every (pid_n, pid_oc, pid_hw) tile serialize the OC dimension.
- Make x channels-last (NHWC) so the IC-K dimension of the GEMM is contiguous, enabling wider vectorized loads on the `tl.dot` K-axis and better coalescing for the spatial gather.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as scatter-add ConvTranspose2d (the natural form): one program per `(n, ic-tile, ih-tile, iw-tile)`, compute outer product `input_tile (IC×HW) ^T @ weight (IC×OC×KH×KW)` and scatter into the output grid. Fuse the spatial mean by accumulating per-`(n, oc)` partial sums in registers/shared memory and only atomic-adding once per program — avoids materializing the (N, OC, 514, 514) output entirely.
- Alternatively, since the mean collapses H,W and KH=KW=3 is tiny, write a direct kernel where each program owns a `(n, oc-tile)` and loops over all `(ih, iw, kh, kw, ic)`, accumulating the pooled scalar directly. The K-loop is `IC*KH*KW = 576`, the spatial loop is `IH*IW = 262144`; with one program per `(n, oc)` you get N*OC = 2048 programs — plenty of parallelism, zero atomics, no intermediate buffer.
- Fuse the entire pipeline (conv_t-pool + bias add + logsumexp + ×10) into a two-stage design: stage-1 produces the (N,OC) pooled tensor in fp32 (no atomics), stage-2 a single-program-per-N reduce. Current finalize is already cheap; the win is removing the atomic_add traffic and over-tiling along HW.
